title: Multi-region routing & control-plane failover playbook (working notes)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working architecture + runbook hybrid covering expected failure modes for the control plane and request routing across multiple regions. Goal is to provide an operational checklist and decision tree engineers can follow during incidents, and to capture architecture rationale for future automation.

Scope:
- Global control-plane components: API gateway, control-plane API servers, config store (etcd), leader-election, routing-policy service, heartbeats.
- Regional components: regional routers (ingress), model-serving clusters, edge proxies, health-check aggregators.
- Traffic routing policies: latency-based, cost-tiered, customer-pin, capacity-aware.

High-level assumptions:
- Each region runs a local routing agent that receives global policy and reports capacity metrics to the control plane every 10s.
- Control-plane state is stored in a quorum-backed etcd cluster spanning two primary and one arbiter (eventual plan to move to three full voting members).
- Failover uses: primary->secondary region; fallbacks to lower-cost model variants if capacity constrained.

Key metrics to watch (dashboards):
- Control-plane API error rate (5m/1m)
- etcd leader term changes / election count
- Routing-policy delta apply latency (time between policy publish and agents ack)
- Regional healthscore (avg latency p50/p95, token throughput, memory/CPU on serving nodes)
- Unroutable requests (%) and fallback-activation rate

Incident scenarios + runbook steps:
1) Control-plane API errors (500s) across regions
- Triage: check control-plane pods in primary region: kubectl -n controlplane get pods -o wide; check restart counts.
- Check etcd health: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=$ENDPOINT endpoint health; if unhealthy, check logs for tombstones / disk pressure.
- If leader flapping: capture leader history (etcdctl endpoint status) and increase logging.
- Short mitigation: scale control-plane API replicas (kubectl scale deployment/controlplane-api --replicas=5) if resource saturation.
- If etcd quorum lost and cannot be recovered: follow emergency restore (see Confluence-ETCD-DR) - caution: data loss risk. Consider redirecting routing agents to a standby read-only control-plane (see below).
- Communication: post summary to #platform-ops with runbook steps taken, time, and link to incident channel.

2) Routing policy publish delay / agents not acking
- Check policy-service logs and the outgoing queue. Run: curl -s http://policy-service:8080/queue | jq .pending
- If queue growth is due to slow downstream (network / proxy), confirm network ACLs and NAT gateway metrics.
- Short mitigation: enable policy diff mode: publish minimal override (critical-fallback) to force immediate agent fallback to safe-policy. Command: /scripts/publish-fallback.sh --policy-id critical-fallback
- If a specific region not acking: SSH to regional agent leader, run agent diag: /opt/router/diag.sh --status. Look for time skew, TLS handshake errors.

3) Region-wide network partition (region R loses connectivity to control plane)
- Detect: regional agent stops reporting; control-plane dashboard shows drop in heartbeats.
- Runbook: automatic behavior should have regional routers enter 'graceful autonomous mode' serving pinned customers allowed in local cache for up to 20 minutes. Confirm autonomous mode active: GET /agents/$REGION/state -> returns autonomous: true.
- Manual: if autonomous mode not triggered, force switch by publishing local policy: POST /policy/localize --region=$R --ttl=20m.
- If region cannot reach other regions for failover, ensure can serve pinned customers by routing to local smaller instances. Notify CS teams for impacted customers.

4) Cross-region routing loop / mis-route (policy bug)
- Symptoms: requests bounce between regions or zig-zag, p50 latency spikes across multiple regions.
- Triage: capture request traces (trace-id) and inspect routing decisions in trace. Use /traces/lookup?trace_id=... to get path.
- Mitigation: immediately apply emergency circuit-breaker policy to stop cross-region routing: /policy/enact --id circuit-breaker-global --action block-cross-region=true.
- Rollback: identify policy commit that caused loop (policy-service accepts last-commit id). Use git history of policy-repo to revert and re-publish safe commit.

5) Capacity shortage in a primary region (headroom exhausted)
- Auto-behavior: routing engine should shift new requests to secondary region based on capacity scoring. Verify by checking routing decisions stream.
- If automatic shifting isn't happening: check scoring service (score-service logs), confirm capacity signals reported by regional agents. If missing, manual override: update routing weight for region X -> reduce to 0.4 (POST /routing/weights).
- Consider applying model-variant fallback to smaller quantized model for non-enterprise customers: POST /model-routing/fallback --percent=30 --variants=[q4_0,q8_0].

Standby control-plane / read-only fallback mode (short description):
- We maintain a warm standby control-plane in secondary region with config sync of last-known-good policy every minute. In DR events, we promote standby to read-only mode for agents to continue reading policy without writes. Promotion steps: 1) verify standby etcd has consistent snapshot, 2) flip DNS to standby endpoints in global gw ttl (script: scripts/promote-standby.sh), 3) disable writes in console (feature flag).
- Note: promotion must be announced to legal & CS if it crosses data residency boundaries.

Communication matrix & escalation:
- Pager callouts: primary on-call (platform) -> if unresolved 15m -> senior on-call -> if unresolved 30m -> eng lead + infra manager -> 60m -> exec on-call.
- Slack channels: #platform-ops (incident coord), #oncall-platform (pager), #status-updates (customer-facing updates).
- Customer comms template: short title, impacted regions, mitigation in progress, ETA for next update, workaround. Link templates in linked_artifacts section.

Post-incident tasks (quick bullets):
- Root cause hypothesis, timeline of key events, commits/policy changes that correlate.
- Follow-ups: increase policy publish ack telemetry, add synthetic test for policy propagation with <=15s SLA, harden etcd disk watermark alerts.
- Automation TODOs: automatic standby promotion, policy publish rollback button, gating for cross-region policy merges.

Appendix: quick commands and helpful endpoints:
- Check agent heartbeat: curl http://controlplane.internal/api/agents/heartbeats | jq '.regions["us-west1"]'
- Force publish fallback policy: /scripts/publish-fallback.sh --policy critical-fallback
- Promote standby: /scripts/promote-standby.sh --confirm
- Capture recent policy commits: git -C /srv/policy-repo log --since='24 hours' --pretty=oneline | head -n 20

Open questions / TODO (working):
- Move to 3-voter etcd cluster vs single arbiter — schedule risk assessment.
- Add synthetic for cross-region loop detection.
- Define exact retention policy for standby policies (how stale is safe?).

Notes to self: keep this doc short and link to Confluence for deep-dive playbooks. Use this file as the 'on-the-floor' steps for first responders.
